pōmĕrīdĭānus (postm- ), a, um, adj. post-meridianus,
I.in the afternoon, post-meridian: “impetratum est a consuetudine, ut peccare suavitatis causā liceret, et pomeridianus quadrigas quam postmeridianus libentius dixerim,” Cic. Or. 47, 157 : “pomeridianum tempus,” id. de Or. 3, 5, 17 ; “also: postmeridianum tempus,” id. Tusc. 3, 3, 7 : “dies,” Sen. Ep. 7, 3, 1 : “horae,” Suet. Gram. 24 : “gnomonis umbra,” Vitr. 1, 6 : “pomeridiana sessio (opp. ambulatio antemeridiana),” Cic. de Or. 3, 30, 121 : “litterae,” id. Att. 12, 53 fin.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
